rounds.proof_sketch: momentum is only used in update_running_stats_kernel, which runs AFTER output is computed (using batch_mean/batch_var) in training mode. In inference mode, momentum isn't used. The mutation affects state updates (running_mean/running_var) that would only be observable in subsequent forward passes.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes momentum from 0.1 to 0.101, but this parameter only affects the exponential moving average update of running statistics in training mode. Critically, the actual output tensor in training mode is computed using batch statistics (batch_mean, batch_var) computed fresh from the input, NOT the running statistics. The running stats update happens after output computation and only affects future inference passes. In inference mode, momentum is not used at all - the output directly uses pre-existing running_mean and running_var. Thus, within any single forward pass, the output is identical regardless of momentum value.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under single-forward-pass testing. Would require: (1) run training forward pass to update running stats with different momentum, (2) run inference forward pass to observe difference in output. This is outside the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: For testing stateful modules like BatchNorm, mutation testing frameworks should support multi-pass test scenarios that exercise state updates (training pass) followed by state usage (inference pass). Mutations to momentum, learning rates, or similar EMA parameters require stateful testing protocols.
